stem: Under current Massachusetts Policy 2024-05, which Schedule II/III prescriptions may qualify for up to a 90-day supply when otherwise lawful? Select all that apply.

explanation.core_reasoning: Current Massachusetts policy allows up to 90 days for OUD drugs and non-opioid Schedule II/III drugs, while ordinary Schedule II/III opioids remain capped at 30 days.

choice_analysis.A: Testosterone is a non-opioid Schedule III example.
choice_analysis.B: OUD treatment drugs are an express category.
choice_analysis.C: Other S-II/III opioids remain subject to the 30-day maximum.
choice_analysis.D: Non-opioid S-II/III drugs can use the 90-day category.
choice_analysis.E: This Schedule II stimulant is a non-opioid.

related_facts: The policy also recognizes implantable infusion-pump prescriptions.
explanation.mpje_trap: Assuming every Schedule II drug shares the same Massachusetts quantity cap.

reasoning_steps: Classify each drug as Schedule II/III
Identify OUD treatment or non-opioid category
